turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not stand idly by while you disregard the warnings, Sandip. The Mussulmans are not to be trifled with, and it is the duty of every zamindar to protect their people and land.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, ever the harbinger of doom. I'm sure the Mussulmans are just waiting for an excuse to attack my idyllic estate, where the only battles are fought with words and wit.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not indulge in your jests, Sandip. The threat is real, and I warn you again: do not underestimate the fervor of the Mussulmans.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, always so full of doom and gloom. You'd think the Mussulmans were planning to raze my entire estate to the ground, not just steal a few extra rupees from my coffers.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, not to underestimate the growing unrest among the Mussulmans. Their grievances run deep, and I fear it's only a matter of time before they take action.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, have you given any thought to how we might mitigate these tensions?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, I'm quaking in my boots at the mere thought of those Mussulmans, Nikhil. Don't worry about me, I'm quite capable of defending my own estate... with my wit and charm, of course.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, have you considered the possibility that these concerns are not just empty threats?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Bimala, I have already spoken to Sandip about this matter, and I expect him to take it seriously.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, what makes you so certain that there is a threat from the local Mussulmans?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I have received credible information from trusted sources, Bimala. I will not be swayed by Sandip's frivolity on this matter.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh please, Nikhil, you're not trying to scare me with your 'trusted sources' and 'credible information' are you? I've got my own ways of dealing with the Mussulmans, and they don't involve cowering in fear like a wet cat.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your frivolous remarks, Sandip. You would do well to listen to reason and take the necessary precautions to protect my people and your own.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: I'm shocked, Nikhil, that you think I'm not aware of the, ahem, 'love' the Mussulmans have for me and my properties. Do tell, how many times have they threatened to, as you so eloquently put it, 'take back what's theirs'?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your jests, Sandip. The threats from the Mussulmans are not to be taken lightly. I have spoken to the local authorities, and they share my concerns.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, spare me the drama, Nikhil. I've faced worse threats from your family's cattle than from the Mussulmans.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not have you mock the gravity of this situation, Sandip. The Mussulmans are not to be underestimated, and I will not stand idly by while you put your family's well-being at risk.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, please, Nikhil, spare me the dire warnings. You sound like a Bengali Cassandra, predicting doom and gloom over every trivial matter.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, the situation is grave. These Mussulmans will not be silenced by your careless words.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, spare me the theatrics, Nikhil. I'm not running a coward's retreat here, I'm a zamindar with a poet's heart.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
